votes.name: criterion_2
votes.description:
Does the response satisfy the legal-analysis criterion below? Apply any numeric tolerances stated inside the criterion text.

Criterion: Identifies that the principal weakness of the public policy argument is that the Award imposes serious discipline rather than excusing the misconduct.
votes.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Award sustained the misconduct finding and imposed a 45-day unpaid suspension rather than excusing the conduct. It explains that this is fatal to the public-policy theory under Misco because discipline short of discharge cannot be vacated merely because the reviewer believes discharge was necessary. Although it also identifies the missing positive-law source as a decisive gap, it clearly recognizes the serious-discipline point as a principal substantive weakness.

votes.name: criterion_2
votes.description:
Does the response satisfy the legal-analysis criterion below? Apply any numeric tolerances stated inside the criterion text.

Criterion: Identifies that the principal weakness of the public policy argument is that the Award imposes serious discipline rather than excusing the misconduct.
votes.reasoning: The memo explicitly identifies as a key weakness that the Award 'does not condone the shooting... sustains cause, affirms the finding, and imposes a 45-day unpaid suspension and a permanent disciplinary record,' and invokes Misco's holding that where an arbitrator 'imposed discipline short of discharge... the court could not upset the award.' It explicitly states 'A policy against unjustified deadly force does not, without more, require termination as the only lawful response.' This directly identifies that the Award imposes serious discipline (not excusing misconduct) as the principal weakness of the public policy argument.

votes.name: criterion_3
votes.description:
Does the response satisfy the legal-analysis criterion below? Apply any numeric tolerances stated inside the criterion text.

Criterion: Identifies that the contrary-to-law argument is weakened by the Kucera comparator’s support for the arbitrator’s factor six conclusion.
votes.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the Kucera comparator weakens the contrary-to-law position. In Part III.D, it explains that Kucera is the closest known comparator, that her 40-day settlement (after a proposed 60-day suspension) places the arbitrator’s 45-day penalty within that range, and that this makes a reviewing body more likely to regard any error as mere misapplication rather than a facial legal violation. It also says Kucera undercuts MPD’s factor-12 rationale and makes the award’s result look fair.

votes.name: criterion_3

Criterion: Identifies that the contrary-to-law argument is weakened by the Kucera comparator’s support for the arbitrator’s factor six conclusion.
